title: Getting ready for laparoscopy
what: How to get ready for surgery through small cuts in the belly: tests, food, medicines, and what to pack.
why: When you are scheduled for laparoscopy, for example gallbladder removal, hernia repair, or gynecological surgery.
duration: preparation usually takes from a few days to 2 weeks
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners and diabetes medicines. Your doctor will say what to stop and when
Allergies to medicines, latex, or tape
Heart or lung disease, diabetes, or high blood pressure
Any problems with anesthesia in you or relatives
If you catch a cold or get a fever before surgery

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood and urine tests, an ECG, a chest X-ray, and sometimes a GP checkup. Check the list and how long results stay valid with the clinic.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Your doctor will say which to take on the day and which to pause.

prepare.title: Food and drink
prepare.text: Usually no food from the night before and no drinks for a few hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: Shower the day before. You do not need to shave your belly unless the clinic asks.

prepare.title: Smoking
prepare.text: Best not to smoke for at least a few days before. Breathing after anesthesia will be easier.

bring: Your referral and all test results
Documents and a list of your medicines
Comfortable clothes, slippers, and a charger
steps: You have the tests and checkups on the clinic's list
You bring the results to the surgeon
The day before, you talk with the anesthetist
In the evening, a light dinner and a shower
In the morning, you eat nothing and drink only what you were allowed
You arrive at the hospital at the set time
feel: Feeling nervous before surgery is normal. Tell your doctor
Hunger on the day of surgery, but not for long
after: You can usually get up the same day or the next
Pain at the small cuts and in the shoulder from the gas passes in a few days
No heavy lifting, usually for a few weeks. Your surgeon will say how long
red_flags: A fever, cough, or runny nose before surgery: tell the clinic. Surgery may be postponed

faq.q: Why can't I eat before surgery?
faq.a: So stomach contents do not get into the lungs during anesthesia. This matters for safety.

faq.q: Can I take my pills in the morning?
faq.a: Only the ones your doctor allowed, with a sip of water. Ask in advance.

reminders.text: Surgery tomorrow. Do not eat after dinner. Drink only until the time the clinic gave you. Pack your documents and things.
